issues.issue: The counterparty may reject a Principal it determines "in its sole discretion" to be unacceptable, an unbounded power to unwind a concluded Transaction. The clause gives no standard against which that determination can be tested.
The removal of any right of setoff against the Agent pulls against the unrestricted setoff and netting rights conferred by Paragraph 12 (Single Agreement).
Paragraph 4(a)-(b) of the Agreement calculates margin on an aggregate basis across all Transactions, whereas this subparagraph requires a Transaction-by-Transaction determination.
Treating each Principal as party to a separate Agreement for default remedies cuts against the cross-Transaction default and netting premise of Paragraph 12 (Single Agreement).

Deeming both Agent and Principals "parties" and treating an Act of Insolvency of the Agent as an Event of Default of the Principal is difficult to reconcile with Annex IV §3(a), which says the Agent does not guarantee its Principal's performance.

"Forward Exposure" is a hypothetical replacement-cost loss "determined in accordance with market practice" where the parties have not agreed otherwise, with no method, source or determining party specified.

Collateral must be "reasonably acceptable to the In-the-Money-Party" and sufficient by Market Value to eliminate an exposure that is itself only measurable by market practice, so the size and adequacy of a call are both left at large.

An Event of Default arises on failure to perform "any covenant or obligation" under "Paragraph 2 or any other provision of this Annex", a catch-all with no materiality filter sitting behind a single specific cross-reference.

Liquidation of Forward Collateral is governed by "in a recognized market (or otherwise in a commercially reasonable manner) at such price or prices as the nondefaulting party may reasonably deem satisfactory", the same open-textured standard used for Purchased Securities, and by a price from an unnamed "generally recognized source". Whether a given sale or mark meets it is contestable on the words alone.

The purchase of Replacement Securities is at prices the nondefaulting party "may reasonably deem satisfactory", or at a deemed price obtained from "a generally recognized source" in its "sole discretion", so the defaulting party's liability is fixed by a standard with no external anchor.

The parties deem all Forward Collateral to be "instruments traded in a recognized market" and allow the nondefaulting party to fix a pricing source "in its sole discretion", which is both a counterfactual premise and an unbounded discretion.

The provision preserves the right to give notice under "subparagraph (a), (b), (c) or (d) of Paragraph 2", but only subparagraph (a) of Annex V Paragraph 2 actually provides for the giving of a notice.
This clause makes Annex VI prevail over "any other term of the Agreement", while Annex I §2 makes Annex I govern over any inconsistency with the Agreement; each purports to trump the other.

The whole operation of the paragraph turns on whether including Accrued Interest is "contrary to market practice with respect to the Securities", an undefined external test that switches between two different pricing formulas.

This section disapplies Paragraph 5 of the Agreement to Buy/Sell Back Transactions and reverses the flow of Income, which cannot be reconciled with Annex I §3, a provision that mandates Buyer transfer Income to Seller under Paragraph 5(i).
The clause reads "In 11 of the Agreement", omitting the word "Paragraph", so the reference must be supplied by inference.

"Fund" is defined by reference to the investment companies "identified on Schedule VII.A", but Schedule VII.A in this executed instrument names no Fund and no Custodian, so the Annex declared applicable by Annex I §1 has no subject.
This sentence gives Annex VII priority over "any other term of the Agreement" while Annex I §2 gives Annex I priority over any inconsistent term of the Agreement, leaving no way to rank the two.

Applying margin and the single-agreement provisions "based solely upon Transactions entered into by a particular Fund" directly negates Paragraph 12's premise that all Transactions form one contractual relationship with cross-Transaction netting.

The flat denial of setoff between Funds contradicts Paragraph 12(ii) of the Agreement, which entitles each party to set off claims in respect of any Transaction against obligations under any other Transaction.

The Buyer's Margin Percentage is left as a blank "at least _%" while the proviso says it may in no event be less than 100%, so the operative figure is missing and the two limbs of the sentence do not fit together. The second sentence then fixes the "Buyer's" Margin Percentage for Transactions in which the Fund is Seller, apparently in place of the Seller's Margin Percentage.
Delivery must be to the Custodian "designated for such Fund in Schedule VII.A", yet Schedule VII.A designates no Custodian, so the mechanic cannot be performed as written.

The Schedule states that the Agreement "is entered into by or on behalf of the following Funds" but the table of Funds and Custodians is blank, which cannot be squared with Annex VII's definition of "Fund" or with Annex I §1 declaring Annex VII and this Schedule applicable.
